title: Research notes: Col. Thomas Marshall at Buck Pond
summary: Sources for Thomas Marshall’s Revolutionary service, his 1783 surveyor appointment, Buck Pond, and his Kentucky politics. Buck Pond Farm’s own history and Wikipedia disagree on who appointed him.

items.text: Colonel, 3rd Virginia Regiment; Brandywine, Germantown, Valley Forge; surrendered at Charleston 1780; first Kentucky visit while on parole.
1783: surveyor general of Kentucky lands due Virginia Continental Line officers and soldiers; office in Lexington.
Buck Pond Farm says Washington appointed him surveyor general of the lands of Fayette County. Treated as contested: Washington was not president in 1783.
Founded 1783; house completed 1785; turned over to son Dr. Louis Marshall about 1800; six generations of Marshalls lived there.
Family moved from Fauquier County to Kentucky in 1785.
Brief’s ‘Federal-style house’ wording was cut: neither source describes the style.
Virginia House of Delegates for Fayette, 1787–1788; delegate to the 1788 Danville convention; Federalist; later federal revenue collector for Kentucky.
Opposed slavery in Ohio but practiced and proposed indentured servitude of formerly enslaved people.

timeline.event: Surrendered at Charleston; on parole, first visit to Kentucky.
Surveyor general of Virginia military lands in Kentucky; Buck Pond founded.
House completed; family moves to Kentucky.
Buck Pond passed to Dr. Louis Marshall (about).
